blocking_findings.location: kernel/kernel.py validate_export (around lines 179-243); pinned scripts/predict_run.py output path (around lines 183-246)
blocking_findings.finding: The recovery consumer hashes the full NPY and validates header, shape, dtype, exact binary length, checkpoint/split metadata, and ordered row groups, but it never rejects NaN or infinity values. The pinned predictor writes and hashes the float32 memmap without a finiteness check. A non-finite fresh export can therefore receive state=validated and contribute to terminal.complete.
blocking_findings.consequence: The required fresh-export acceptance evidence is incomplete even though checkpoint bytes and prediction-file identity are bound.
blocking_findings.smallest_fix: In a new packet identity, scan the produced NPY by memory map in bounded row/chunk slices with isfinite before marking the job validated; persist finite=true and checked element count in the export receipt. Keep the original R1 packet immutable.

additional_findings.finding: terminal_inventory.json is written before reference_prediction_hashes is added to the terminal object. The expected historical NPY hashes and collected hashes are saved only in status.json, not the terminal inventory.
additional_findings.consequence: A terminal inventory reader cannot see the intended expected-versus-collected comparison without also reading status.json. The worker still records the map in status, so this is a completeness gap rather than evidence of bad predictions.
additional_findings.smallest_fix: In a new packet identity, compute reference_prediction_hashes after the output file list is hashed but before serializing terminal_inventory.json; then save the same terminal object into status.json. Do not require equality with the old device's NPY hash; record equal/different.

additional_findings.finding: The reviewed packet files match all eight entries in PACKET_MANIFEST_R1.json, but the packet directory itself was untracked in the actor worktree at review time.
additional_findings.consequence: The content hashes identify the reviewed bytes, but no commit currently freezes those files in the packet worktree.
additional_findings.smallest_fix: Commit the reviewed packet files after corrections and publish the resulting commit and regenerated manifest digest before any provider handoff.

The R3 source manifest/job contract pins scripts/predict_run.py at SHA-256 afc5aaaef7edd78f4b719a6be450b10d82aefcbf497b4515f684f51930e229f9; the local file has the same digest. The recovery filters each bound source job to its original exact `predict_run.py RUN valid --epoch E` export argv and uses the original per-export 1,800-second limits. No fit command remains in the worker plan; packet manifest declares zero fit and three export commands.

The worker checks the requested two-T4 allocation, source-bundle digest and member source hashes, fold-0 asset/portable registry/raw-data footer identities, split-manifest digest, propensity cache metadata/layout, rescued archive identity, fresh NPY full-byte SHA/header/shape/dtype/length, sidecar checkpoint/split/run/epoch bindings and valid row order. The expected shape is (1873, 20000, 2) float32; recovery writes only the six exact run-specific prediction/sidecar files into out/predictions and inventories their bytes and hashes.

No worker execution, fit, GPU use, upload, provider mutation or scoring was performed by this review. The recovery output NPYs do not yet exist, so fresh-output finiteness and post-export collection could not be exercised here.
